openness: You look into claims that contradict what you believed — the habit that starves narrative capture before it forms.
You can hold questions open, which starves manufactured urgency of its power.
conscientiousness: You check before sharing even when hurried — the habit the misinformation research ties to sharing fewer false claims.
You track where your claims came from, so retraction and correction stay possible.
extraversion: Your networks surface second opinions fast when you ask for them.
You talk decisions through, which catches what solo reasoning misses.
agreeableness: You give people the benefit of the doubt, which keeps scrutiny specific rather than paranoid.
Cooperative habits make real verification networks work.
emotional-stability: You can wait before reacting to upsetting content, which defeats emotion-timed bait.
Criticism does not easily move your read of the facts.
fairness-reciprocity: You check what the other side gets from a deal that favors you.
You can refuse or return a gift that came with strings.

urgency.label: Manufactured urgency
urgency.tacticFamily: False deadlines, last-chance framing, one-shot windows
urgency.watchpoint: When a deadline appears suddenly, check whether the deadline itself is the technique before it sets your schedule.
urgency.countermeasure: If a deadline appears, restate the claim out loud and verify one independent source before responding.

authority.label: Authority presentation
authority.tacticFamily: Fake credentials, spoofed senders, letterhead and form-number mimicry
authority.watchpoint: Official-looking format is presentation, not verification. Spoofed authority counts on exactly this reflex.
authority.countermeasure: If authority is claimed, name the credential and check it at the primary source, out of band.

social-approval.label: Consensus pressure
social-approval.tacticFamily: Astroturfing, social proof, everyone-agrees framing, ostracism threats
social-approval.watchpoint: Unanimity is cheap to fake. The more a group seems to agree, the more worth checking who is actually doing the agreeing.
social-approval.countermeasure: If everyone is said to agree, find one named dissenter and their reasons before deciding.

scarcity.label: Scarcity and FOMO
scarcity.tacticFamily: Manufactured shortage, exclusion framing, others-already-have-it comparison
scarcity.watchpoint: Scarcity reframes 'is this good?' as 'will I miss it?' — and the second question is much easier to manipulate.
scarcity.countermeasure: If it may run out, decide what you would choose if it did not, then compare.

conflict.label: Conflict and aggression
conflict.watchpoint: Sharp tone can be a pressure tactic rather than an argument. A concession made only to end a conversation skips the verification the decision deserved.
conflict.countermeasure: If conflict spikes, defer the decision by one day by default. Sharpness is not new information.

isolation.label: Isolation and secrecy
isolation.tacticFamily: Keep-this-between-us, special-selection flattery, cutting off other perspectives
isolation.watchpoint: Being asked to keep something secret is itself the flag. Isolation works by making the secret feel like a bond.
isolation.countermeasure: If you are asked to keep it secret, name one trusted person you will tell. Secrecy requested is a signal received.
isolation.note: If isolation appears in a close relationship alongside control or threats, use the support path in DESIGN-personal-defense-profile.md §8 — no drill substitutes for a human conversation.

fatigue.label: Fatigue and cognitive load
fatigue.tacticFamily: Late-night persuasion, long-winded pressure, decision fatigue exploitation
fatigue.watchpoint: Tired judgment answers on tone instead of content. Irreversible decisions made exhausted are the ones you are most likely to regret.
fatigue.countermeasure: If you are worn down, no irreversible decisions: schedule the reply for when you have slept.

disconfirmationPrompt: Record one example that does not fit this picture. A pattern you can disconfirm is evidence; one you cannot is decoration.
evidenceNote: This map is built from your own answers and logged events. The countermeasures come from technique-recognition research (inoculation trials, accuracy-prompt meta-analyses); the lens layer is dimensional self-report, which is noisy and context-dependent. Nothing here is a trait prediction or a manipulability score — the same verification toolkit works for every profile, and your observation log decides which watchpoints actually apply to you.

supportCard.title: This looks bigger than a technique
supportCard.body: Enforced secrecy, isolation, threats, or control over money, movement, or contact are coercive-control markers, not persuasion tactics. A drill cannot assess danger. Tell one trusted person, and contact local professional or emergency support. This card routes to human help on purpose.
